en: The clear coconut water inside a young buko is a liquid, while its white meat is a solid.
Exposing a wet iron roof in Tacloban to salty sea air causes it to chemically change into rust.
A bowl of halo-halo containing shaved ice, sweet beans, jelly, and leche flan is a heterogeneous mixture.
Dissolving Muscovado sugar from Negros into hot water creates a homogeneous liquid mixture known as a solution.
Squeezing a calamansi to extract its juice for cooking is an example of a physical change.
Pumice stones formed from volcanic eruptions in Taal are less dense than water, which allows them to float.
Exposing sweet tuba to air allows microorganisms to chemically change it into sour coconut vinegar through fermentation.
Artisanal miners in Benguet can hammer raw gold into thin sheets because gold is highly malleable.
The hot steam rising from a boiling pot of sinigang is water in its gaseous state.
Fishermen in Pampanga use fine nets to separate a physical mixture of small fish from muddy water.
Electrical grids in Manila use copper wires because copper is an excellent conductor of electricity.
Burning dried Carabao mango leaves in a backyard produces ash and smoke, indicating a chemical change.
